summary.headline: Best UK opportunity today: receivables and e-invoicing automation for SMEs, with MTD onboarding still a close second.
summary.best_opportunity: E-invoicing rollout and cash-collection automation for UK SMEs
summary.why_now: Live GOV.UK signals are unusually strong: the e-invoicing consultation response says 80% of SMEs still mainly use PDF or email invoices and cites 60% to 80% lower invoicing costs plus 20% fewer late payments from adoption, while a 19 May 2026 government announcement says late payments cost the UK economy £11 billion a year. That creates immediate ROI-led sales angles and recurring support revenue.

top_opportunities.name: E-invoicing rollout and receivables automation for SMEs
top_opportunities.description: Sell a fixed-scope setup that standardises invoice creation, automates reminders, tracks disputes and promises to pay, and gives owners a simple overdue-cash dashboard across Xero, QuickBooks or spreadsheet-led workflows.
top_opportunities.why_now: Evidence is strong. The GOV.UK e-invoicing consultation response says 80% of SMEs still mainly send PDF or email invoices and cites 60% to 80% lower invoicing costs, 20% fewer late payments and about £11,300 annual savings for small firms. Separately, a 19 May 2026 GOV.UK announcement says late payments cost the UK economy £11 billion a year.
top_opportunities.buyer: Micro and small B2B service firms, agencies, consultancies, trades businesses and wholesalers
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High - setup fee plus monthly monitoring, reminder automation and reporting
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Excellent for a solo engineer because the wedge is integration, workflow logic and dashboards rather than building a full accounting system.
risks: Some buyers will assume their accounting package already solves invoicing unless the pitch is framed around debtor days and collected cash
Messy billing data and inconsistent internal processes can slow onboarding
top_opportunities.verdict: Best overall today because the pain is immediate cashflow, the ROI is easy to quantify, and the service can start manually before any software build-out.

top_opportunities.name: Making Tax Digital onboarding and quarterly-support automation
top_opportunities.description: Offer a productized package that checks MTD eligibility, cleans records, connects bookkeeping software, sets reminder workflows and handles quarterly support for sole traders, landlords and small accountancy firms.
top_opportunities.why_now: Evidence is strong. Current GOV.UK guidance says qualifying income above £50,000 for the 2024 to 2025 tax year must use MTD for Income Tax from 6 April 2026, above £30,000 from 6 April 2027 and above £20,000 from 6 April 2028. That means live migration work now and recurring support afterwards.
top_opportunities.buyer: Sole traders, landlords, independent bookkeepers and small accountancy practices
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High - onboarding fee plus monthly or quarterly support
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Excellent for a solo engineer because the first sale is implementation and admin reduction, not a full accounting product.
risks: Accounting software vendors already own the ledger, so the wedge must be onboarding, cleanup and workflow support
Avoid crossing into regulated tax advice and stay positioned as implementation and process support
top_opportunities.verdict: Still one of the best UK solo opportunities because the trigger is live, the budget is low and recurring support is built in.

top_opportunities.name: AI document drafting and workflow automation for small professional firms
top_opportunities.description: Build narrow automations that turn calls, forms and notes into first-draft reports, letters, summaries and internal checklists for firms that produce structured documents all day.
top_opportunities.why_now: Evidence is good but less direct than the top two. The current GOV.UK AI Opportunities Action Plan says AI assistants can free up to 20% of an employee's time and that drafting structured reports and forms can cut final document production times by 20% to 80% in professional services. That supports ROI-led offers for document-heavy SMEs.
top_opportunities.buyer: Accountants, mortgage brokers, planning consultants, surveyors, recruiters and compliance-heavy niche agencies
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High - setup plus monthly usage, maintenance and prompt/workflow tuning
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Very strong for a solo engineer who can package LLM workflows, document templates and approval steps into one managed service.
risks: Buying urgency is weaker than compliance or late-payment pain, so demos and measured time savings matter
Hallucination and data-handling concerns mean human review must stay in the loop
top_opportunities.verdict: Best AI-native option if sold as a narrow workflow product for one document-heavy niche rather than generic AI consulting.

top_opportunities.name: Cyber Essentials readiness and evidence-collection automation
top_opportunities.description: Sell a standard package covering MFA, device checks, access hygiene, backup checks, staff guidance and evidence collection so small organisations can reach or renew Cyber Essentials faster.
top_opportunities.why_now: Evidence is solid. The current GOV.UK Cyber Essentials overview says over 215,000 certificates have been awarded, including 49,248 in the past 12 months, and says an up-to-date certificate enables a business to bid for government contracts where financial or personal data is involved. That supports a checklist-driven recurring service.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small professional firms, agencies, clinics, charities and B2B suppliers handling sensitive data
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Medium to high - annual renewals, monitoring and periodic checks
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good if you prefer technical delivery and keep the offer tightly standardised.
risks: Trust matters in security work, so some buyers will prefer established specialists
Bespoke security consulting can quickly break the part-time solo model
top_opportunities.verdict: A credible productized service if you keep scope narrow and sell speed-to-certification rather than broad cybersecurity consulting.

top_opportunities.name: Tender monitoring and bid-drafting assistant for SME suppliers
top_opportunities.description: Create a focused tool or managed service that monitors relevant tenders, flags fit, drafts first-pass answers and stores reusable evidence, pricing and compliance content.
top_opportunities.why_now: Evidence is decent. The Procurement Act 2023 learning materials on GOV.UK say the Act contains benefits for SMEs and VCSEs, aims to remove barriers to new entrants and improve transparency and visibility of opportunities. That makes a narrow tender-monitoring and bid-support layer plausible, though demand is less immediate than payment or tax pain.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small consultancies, agencies, specialist service firms and compliance-heavy B2B suppliers
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Medium to high - retainer, seat fee or managed bid support
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good for an engineer who can combine scraping, matching, document generation and workflow management into one narrow offer.
risks: Tender demand is episodic, so revenue can be lumpier than invoicing or compliance services
The evidence for urgency is real but weaker than the top opportunities, so niche positioning is important
top_opportunities.verdict: Worth pursuing only with a tight niche, such as one supplier category or framework type, not the whole procurement market.

best_pick.name: E-invoicing rollout and receivables automation for SMEs
best_pick.why_it_wins: It hits the user's core constraints best: it can be sold fast as a service, starts with low tooling cost, addresses immediate pain tied to cash collection, and naturally expands into monthly recurring monitoring and workflow support. The live UK evidence is stronger than for most generic AI offers.
validation_plan: Pick one buyer segment first, such as agencies, trades firms or small consultancies, and map their current invoice-to-cash process in detail.
Build a tiny demo that shows invoice creation, automated reminders, dispute tracking and an overdue-cash dashboard using existing accounting tools and lightweight automation.
Offer a fixed-price pilot to 10 local firms with a promise to reduce overdue invoices or admin hours within 30 days.
Track before-and-after metrics on debtor days, time spent chasing invoices and percentage of invoices paid on time.
best_pick.first_offer: Invoice-to-cash automation setup: connect invoicing source, create reminder sequences, add dispute tracking and deliver a weekly cash-collection dashboard. Charge roughly £299 to £999 setup plus £49 to £199 per month.
best_pick.mvp: A thin internal tool plus Zapier or Make, email templates, webhook-driven reminders and a simple owner dashboard pulling invoice status from one accounting platform.
customer_types: Other UK SMEs with recurring invoicing and overdue debtor pain
best_pick.do_today: Build one vertical landing page, wire up a demo flow on sample invoice data and start direct outreach to 30 UK firms that visibly invoice other businesses.
